author: Thomas Daigle
description: Edward Dubrovsky, a Toronto-area cybersecurity exec arrested by the FBI amid a high-profile hacking probe, colluded with cybercriminals to extort money from his own clients, according to explosive allegations laid out by U.S. prosecutors.
title: Canadian cybersecurity exec arrested by FBI accused of working with criminals to defraud his own clients

author: Jennifer Keiller
description: With the Alberta referendum now in the books, some First Nation chiefs are calling on the provincial government to drop its appeal of a judge’s decision to quash the citizen petition on separation.
title: Chiefs, Opposition call for Alberta government to drop appeal of decision that quashed separation petition

description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.
title: Trump tells South Florida rally that U.S. warships could 'do a little stopover' in Cuba, after Iran

author: Amir Said
description: The Alberta government says new legislation about which flags can be displayed at schools will take effect in January. Those rules include making the Alberta and Canada flags mandatory, and prohibiting flags that "advance a social or political cause."
title: New regulations on flags flown at Alberta schools to take effect in January

author: Natalie Stechyson
description: The new voice for the directions feature on Google Maps started rolling out earlier this year as part of the tech giant's ongoing updates to improve the driving experience and make voice guidance more natural with help from its Gemini chatbot models.
title: Google Maps changed its default voice to be more 'natural.' People hate it

author: Kate McKenna
description: The federal Conservatives are accusing Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada of exaggerating the decrease in new permanent residents in official messaging posted online.
title: Conservatives accuse government of 'cooking the books' over immigration data presentation

author: Arrthy Thayaparan
description: In just his second big league season, Toronto catcher Liam Hicks will make his World Series debut when the Tampa Rays take on the Milwaukee Brewers for Game 1 at 8 p.m. ET Friday.
title: It started with hockey, then he picked up a bat. Meet the Toronto catcher headed to the World Series

description: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy on Friday defended his campaign's ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Amy Acton in the closely watched race for Ohio governor.
title: Vivek Ramaswamy defends campaign ad featuring estranged mother of Amy Acton

author: Jackson Weaver
description: Sixteen years in the making, stop-motion animation company Laika's Wildwood is its single best movie ever.
title: Stop-motion movie Wildwood is a staggering masterpiece. It's a miracle it exists at all

author: Peter Zimonjic
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday criticized a decision to restrict Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's military-grade satellite network, saying the move is costing lives.
title: Ukraine's restricted access to Musk's Starshield is costing lives, Carney says

author: Jeff Lagerquist
description: The CEO of Canada’s largest grocery retailer is apologizing to about two million shoppers for a data breach earlier this year.
title: Loblaw CEO apologizes to 2 million shoppers for personal data hack, offers free credit monitoring
Trump to exempt some Canadian products from tariffs amid midterm pressure

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: Diamonds are forever, but James Bond actors come and go — and the time has come to pick the next 007. Screen tests to choose the star of Amazon MGM's upcoming Bond film are reportedly occurring in London this weekend. Two of the rumoured finalists are Callum Turner and Jack Lowden.
title: James Bond screen tests reportedly happening in London this weekend

author: Daniel Johnson
description: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada says the bigger picture on how much Canadians pay in bank fees might be more murky than it should be, with foreign exchange fees and fees based on usage adding up for less wealthy Canadians in particular.
title: Consumer agency says unclear bank fees can add up for customers

author: John Mazerolle
description: Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid is known for his blistering speed — and so far this year he's also flying up the stats leaderboard at a pace not seen since the days of Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux.
title: Connor McDavid is off to a historic start. Could some of Gretzky's records fall this season?

author: Griffin Jaeger
description: Miley Cyrus flew fan and musician Cash Jacobs — who has Stage 3 breast cancer — to her Los Angeles show to help shave her head. A video of the moment shared online has since surpassed 1.5 million views.
title: Miley Cyrus shaves fan's head after her breast cancer diagnosis

author: Sheena Goodyear
description: Scientists at Stanford University in California stumbled on a promising discovery when two coral fragments in the lab — one bleached and one healthy — tipped over in a tank and touched.
title: Scientists put a dying coral next to a healthy one — and watched it heal before their eyes

author: Anya Zoledziowski
description: MapQuest users in Canada and the U.S. can now see where some surveillance cameras have been set up in their communities.
title: MapQuest now showing surveillance camera locations across Canada, U.S.

author: Darren Bernhardt
description: The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg after the Jets traded the all-star goalie on Friday.
title: The saga is over as Winnipeg Jets trade Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey

description: Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will ‌begin on Oct. 29, the White House said on Friday.
title: Melania Trump brokers humanitarian ceasefire for ravaged Ukraine city Oleshky

author: Lauran Neergaard
description: A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients' tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck.
title: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps cut the chances of melanoma tumor recurrence in major study

author: Darren Major
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is pushing back on the latest round of allegations that Canada could be interfering in the U.S. midterm elections.
title: Claims that Canada is interfering in U.S. midterms have 'no merit,' Carney says

author: Abby Hughes
description: The company says it will add some 800 jobs and has earmarked millions to expand in Kansas, Indiana, Texas and Connecticut. U.S. President Donald Trump indicated the expansion was coming in a social media post on Thursday — after he walked back earlier threats to prevent Bombardier from selling in the U.S.
title: Canadian planemaker Bombardier to spend $270M US expanding in 4 states

description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
title: Europe's killer heat this summer claims record 50,000 lives, study suggests

author: Maggie Kirk
description: Parks Canada is restructuring its workforce following a $145-million budget cut over the next three years. The union representing the public servants said the impending layoffs are "disappointing."
title: Parks Canada plan to cut 500 jobs draws criticism from union

description: Prince Harry's wife, Meghan, said Friday she was "deeply distressed" by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's former home. She also revealed that a letter containing "troubling allegations" about him had been sent to London police in 2018.
title: Meghan says U.K. police advised her of 'disturbing allegations' against her father in 2018

description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
title: Israeli soldiers fatally shoot 2 Palestinians near Hebron. Netanyahu orders West Bank lockdown

author: Ruby Cornish
description: Last month Paige Adamson was stopped at a U.S.-Canada border crossing and interrogated for hours about whether she had unlawfully voted in a U.S. election. She died at home on Sunday after a fall, telling friends she was scared of being detained if she sought medical care.
title: Canadian woman dies in U.S. after fears of detainment prevented her from seeking medical care

author: Maeve Ellis
description: The Prince Albert project reflects a national trend of denser, centrally located housing since the federal government increased incentives a few years ago, an expert says.
title: Developer wants to build 500 modular homes on roof of struggling Sask. mall

author: Murray Brewster
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney defended his government’s pursuit of trade with countries accused of human rights abuses, arguing few nations meet Canada’s standards. Wrapping up a visit to Turkey, Carney insisted engagement does not equal approval, but declined to say whether he personally challenged President Erdogan over his government’s crackdown.
title: Carney defends doing business with countries that don’t share Canada’s values

author: Josh Crabb, Catherine Moreau
description: It took five weeks and cost Winnipeg dads Darrel Nadeau and Mackenzie Dyck about $6,000 to get formally recognized as parents after a surrogate mother gave birth to their son, Théo.
title: Winnipeg couple files complaint over birth registration laws after surrogacy legal hurdles

author: Kendra Seguin
description: A former student of a London private school and parents are concerned that children were under constant video surveillance in the classroom and asked to critique the footage with their peers. The matter is being investigated by Ontario’s privacy commissioner.
title: Ontario private school scrutinized over class video surveillance, making kids watch themselves ‘misbehaving’

author: Lynette Adams
description: “I’m glad this is happening now that I’m in my 50s and not when I was 20,” said actor Willow Kean.
title: Below ... and beyond: What's next for N.L. actor Willow Kean

author: Jorge Barrera
description: Frustrations around corruption and feelings of personal financial stagnation driving voting choices as Brazil heads to presidential run-off on Sunday, Oct. 25.
title: A polarized Brazil heads to presidential vote Sunday with economy, corruption top of mind

author: Geoff Nixon
description: A new World Series champion will be crowned this year, as two of Major League Baseball's most frugal franchises — the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays — battle for supremacy. Here's how they got there and what to expect.
title: How the Brewers and Rays got to baseball's biggest stage with small budgets and small ball

author: Elizabeth Thompson
description: Searches of electronic devices such as phones and laptops of travellers entering the United States are up more than 32 per cent this year and are on track to set a new record, CBC News has learned.
title: Searches of cellphones, laptops by U.S. customs up more than 32% so far this year

author: Helen Surgenor
description: There's big buzz around Yaga, the new Crave show premiering Friday and featuring Hudson Williams in his first major role since Heated Rivalry. But the entire cast of the witchy series is packed with Canadian talent, including Carrie-Anne Moss and stars from Schitt's Creek and Letterkenny. We've got a primer featuring lore from the show and insight from its creator.
title: Yaga, Crave's witchy new show, is full of myth, legend and Canadian stars. Here's what to know before watching
